source: Okta profile update: a full-resource PUT, RFC 7644 section 3.5.1
expect_why: criterion 1 names UPDATE alongside create and deactivate, and the corpus drove neither a PUT nor anything else that replaces a resource. Okta re-sends the whole profile on every change, so this is the shape most of its traffic takes. The userName matches the seeded person because a changed one is refused as immutable, which is a different contract this fixture is not about. THE BODY FRAGMENT IS THE POINT: a review deleted all three of `replace_user`'s effects, leaving a PUT that authenticates, parses and renders the UNCHANGED resource with 200, and a status-only fixture passed. The seeding binds no externalId, so this fragment can only be true if this request rebound one. IT PINS ONE EFFECT OF THREE, and saying so is better than a fragment that looks like it pins more. An `"active":true` fragment was tried and REJECTED: the seeded person is already active (ScimUser::active defaults true and an absent activation row reads active), so it was false-beforehand only because the two deactivate fixtures sort earlier by filename -- a review renamed this file and the guard died. `set_active` and the extension replace are pinned by tests/users.rs, which can assert an ABSENCE where expect_body_contains cannot.
